questions.prompt: How does AI show up in a typical workweek?

options.text: I rarely or never use AI for work.
Occasionally, for drafting, questions, or quick research.
Several times a week across multiple tasks.
Daily across several types of work.
It is embedded across research, analysis, communication, or execution.

questions.prompt: You must review a report, spreadsheet, and supporting documents by tomorrow. What is your approach?

options.text: Review manually, using AI for occasional questions.
Ask AI to summarize individual documents as I go.
Provide the materials together with instructions on what to compare and flag.
Use a repeatable workflow with context, sources, instructions, and validation.
I generally would not use AI for this type of work.

questions.prompt: How does AI get the information needed for your work?

options.text: I type or paste information into a chat.
I upload files or groups of files when needed.
I use persistent workspaces with instructions and source material.
AI can access approved data or tools through integrations.
I rarely use AI with professional information.

questions.prompt: AI identifies a fact or analytical conclusion that could materially affect a financial or business decision. What is your default next step?

options.text: Use it if the explanation sounds reasonable and the model is reputable.
Ask the AI to confirm its answer a second time.
Spot-check the most important part against the underlying material.
Verify the material conclusion against authoritative source information before relying on it.
Use a source-grounded review process that preserves traceability and human judgment for material conclusions.

questions.prompt: What distinguishes an AI agent from a conventional chatbot?

options.text: An agent is simply a chatbot with a larger context window.
It can pursue a goal across steps and use permitted tools or actions.
An agent always works without human review.
An agent is any AI that remembers a previous conversation.
An agent is mainly a chatbot customized with company branding and instructions.

questions.prompt: What most expands AI from a consulted tool into a working system?

options.text: Generating longer responses in a single chat.
Connecting it to approved knowledge and tools for context and permitted actions.
Using a more conversational writing style.
Giving the AI a permanent personality.
Increasing the number of prompts you send each day.

questions.prompt: When an AI output is not good enough, what most closely describes how you improve it?

options.text: I ask it to try again or make the answer better.
I rewrite the request with more detail.
I diagnose what is missing—context, source material, constraints, examples, tools, or intermediate steps—and adjust the approach.
I usually switch to another model and repeat the same request.
I generally stop using AI for that task.

questions.prompt: What does a standard such as Model Context Protocol primarily address?

options.text: It gives every AI model the same personality and writing style.
How AI applications connect to external tools, data, and context.
It is mainly a benchmark for comparing model intelligence.
It is a method for compressing prompts to reduce token usage.
It permanently stores all user conversations in a shared database.

questions.prompt: A weekly task gathers information, analyzes it, formats results, and flags exceptions. How is AI involved?

options.text: It is not meaningfully involved.
I manually prompt AI for one or two steps.
I use a saved prompt, template, or project.
A defined workflow handles most steps with review points.
A triggered workflow uses approved tools, completes steps, and surfaces exceptions.

questions.prompt: AI can read connected documents and use tools. Which risk becomes especially important?

options.text: The AI may use too much punctuation in its responses.
Hidden instructions can manipulate the system, making permissions and validation critical.
The AI will automatically make every connected document public.
Connected tools eliminate the need for source verification because the data is direct.
The main risk is that answers will always become shorter.

questions.prompt: Which best describes the breadth of your current professional AI use?

options.text: Mostly writing, rewriting, or answering questions.
Writing plus research, analysis, or document review.
Several recurring activities across research, analysis, documents, communication, or decision support.
AI participates in a meaningful portion of my professional workflow across several categories of work.
I do not meaningfully use AI professionally yet.

questions.prompt: Which practice best moves beyond one-off prompting?

options.text: Keeping prompts as short as possible so the model has fewer instructions to follow.
Using persistent context, relevant sources, explicit constraints, and structured workflows.
Always asking for the longest possible answer.
Using only one AI model so outputs stay stylistically consistent.
Avoiding files and structured data because language models perform best with plain text only.

questions.prompt: After AI produces something useful, what usually happens next?

options.text: I manually recreate or re-enter the result in the system where it is needed.
I copy/paste or download/upload the result into another application.
I use a standardized export, template, or structured handoff.
Parts of the handoff are integrated so approved information can move between AI and another system with limited manual work.
Where appropriate, the workflow can pass structured results to approved tools/systems and preserve review or approval steps.

questions.prompt: What is the most advanced kind of AI execution you use with any regularity?

options.text: Single prompts or short conversations.
Multi-step work where I manually guide each stage.
Reusable workflows that carry out several defined steps after my initial instruction.
Tool-connected or scheduled workflows that can perform defined actions and return results or exceptions for review.
I do not meaningfully use AI for execution today.

questions.prompt: You want AI to help with confidential or client information. What is your approach?

options.text: If the AI tool is popular, I assume it is appropriate for confidential information.
I remove obvious names and then use whichever AI tool is most convenient.
I assess sensitivity and use approved tools and settings.
I follow applicable policies, data rules, and approved environments.
I combine approved environments, least-necessary access, permissions, and human review.

optional_unscored.prompt: What's the most useful thing you're currently doing with AI at work?
optional_unscored.warning: Optional. Do not include confidential, client, transaction, or proprietary information.
